title: A 41-day GJ 3293 residual has gain ranges that include zero in 62 later HARPS velocities
abstract: We search for extra radial velocity signals in the public 2017 HARPS series of GJ 3293. A search from 2 to 1000 days in 145 early measurements selects a 41.135-day residual after four known planet periods and a linear trend are fitted. The fixed early wave reduces weighted error in 62 later measurements by 17.8 percent. All six conditional 95 percent block ranges include zero. The 30-day training and 30-day test range is -3.5 to 20.9 percent. Three block-sign search tests give conditional tail fractions from 0.068 to 0.242. Adding second harmonics of the known planets reduces the gain to 1.7 percent. The period is close to the known stellar rotation period. Another reduction gives positive point gains but shares 206 exposures. It also shows that a large change in reported line width depends on the data product. These results do not establish a new planet or a new physical cause. The later series spans only 172 days, and the known periods were selected with the full data. Code, exact inputs, source hashes, figures, controls, and offline steps are included.

display.caption: All six conditional gain ranges include zero. Second harmonics of the known planets remove most of the point gain. The ranges do not include frequency selection error.

The early velocity search selects a period near 41 days. Activity scans and the early and later residuals are shown. Activity indices have equal weights because the source table supplies no errors for them.

Same-exposure line widths differ between data products. The later prediction score also changes rapidly with trial period. The marked third harmonic is a possible model confusion, not an identified cause.
